newsitem.title: USA: MetLife to buy Security First for $377 mln.
newsitem.headline: MetLife to buy Security First for $377 mln.

text.p: Metropolitan Life Insurance Co Thursday said it agreed to buy London Insurance Group Inc's Security First Group Inc subsidiary for $377 million in cash.

Security First Group, based in Los Angeles, markets, distributes and underwrites a variety of fixed and variable annuity contracts. Security First primarily serves public employees of schools, universities, states and municipalities through 403(b), 457 and 401(k) plans; and customers of regional and community banks.
The closing of the transaction is subject to regulatory approvals.

"MetLife's acquisition of Security First Group, like our merger with The New England last year, is a strategic transaction that adds significant value to MetLife's core business by extending the company's market reach," said Harry P. Kamen, chairman, president and chief executive officer of MetLife.

Fred Tomczyk, president and chief executive officer of London Insurance Group, said: "Our decision to sell Security First Group was a strategic one. We recognize that Security First Group needed either significant investment to be a larger and lower cost competitor in the increasingly competitive U.S. annuity market, or that it be sold to become part of a larger financial services player in the field."
New York-based MetLife is one of the world's largest financial services companies.
